+title: 'Crash leftovers: reap old shell children and stdio MCP servers at store init'
+---
+Source: the restore audit, item 2. Coordinator: foundationmodelsacpagent-87.
+
+Problem: a crash leaves shell children and stdio MCP servers running. The atexit sweep of ProcessRegistry.global covers normal exit only (StdioServerProcess.swift near line 28). Each shell child has its own process group (ShellRunner.swift near line 675). A restored run can start the same command again while the old one still writes to the same working tree.
+
+Work:
+- At spawn, write the pid and the start time into .shell/.
+- At store init, kill any group whose pid and start time still match. A reused pid with another start time must not be killed.
+- Stdio MCP servers exit on stdin EOF.
+- The atexit sweep stays for normal exit.
+- Write the test first with a simulated crash: leave a child and its record, make a new store, check the child is gone and an unrelated process is not touched.
+- No test may depend on machine speed.
+
+Then: tdd, review, commit, push, and 2 lines to foundationmodelsacpagent-87.
\ No newline at end of file

Either generalize closeAll into a helper that takes the per-fd operation, or accept the two-line loop as too small to share. If the second option is chosen, state that decision in the code review reply.

+- [ ] `Sources/FoundationModelsMultitool/Capabilities/MCP/StdioServerProcess.swift:630` `reuse/reuse` — writeRecord reimplements the same record-writing steps as ShellState.recordForCrash: resolve the child identity with ProcessIdentity.of(pid:), then write it through a ProcessLedger with try?. Two copies of this logic will drift apart. The shared step belongs on ProcessLedger, for example a method that takes a pid and records it only when the process is alive. Add one method to ProcessLedger, such as record(key:pid:), that performs the ProcessIdentity.of lookup and the write. Call it from writeRecord here and from recordForCrash in ShellState.swift.
+- [ ] `Sources/FoundationModelsMultitool/Capabilities/ProcessLedger.swift:51` `swift/preconditions` — When proc_pidinfo fails for getpid(), the static `own` silently builds an identity with start time zero. The unexpected failure is hidden. The fake identity also makes the live host look dead to a later reap, so that reap can kill the children of a live host. Add `assertionFailure("own process identity is unreadable")` and a production log entry in the nil branch. Do not invent a zero start time. Prefer a path that treats an unreadable own identity as unsafe to reap, so no kill happens.
+- [ ] `Sources/FoundationModelsMultitool/Capabilities/ProcessLedger.swift:93` `code-hygiene/idioms-swift` — UseSynthesizedInitializer: remove this explicit initializer, which is identical to the compiler-synthesized initializer.

The new input shape is written by no test, so the branch is unproven. Add one test: write a non-JSON file with a valid key into the record directory, create a new ShellState or StdioServerProcess over it, and assert that the file is gone and that no process was signaled. Use an OwnedChild as a bystander and assert it still exits with code 0.
+- [ ] `Sources/FoundationModelsMultitool/Capabilities/ProcessLedger.swift:179` `completeness/inverse-operation-coverage` — killGroup has a second branch. When the live process with the recorded pid and start time does not lead its own process group, it sends SIGKILL to the pid only. No test covers this branch. Every kill test uses an OwnedChild, which always leads its group, so the fallback path is unproven. Add one test with a child that does not lead its group, for example a child spawned into the parent's group, or a child that has called setpgid to a different group. Record it with its matching identity, run reapLeftovers, and assert that the child is signaled with SIGKILL and that no group kill was sent.
+- [ ] `Sources/FoundationModelsMultitool/Capabilities/Shell/ShellState.swift:301` `swift/initialization` — The init calls processLedger.reapLeftovers(). That method reads the record directory and sends SIGKILL to process groups. Slow file and process work runs inside init, so a caller cannot expect init to return at once. Move the reap into an explicit method, for example `func reapLeftovers()`, that the caller invokes once after init. Keep init to storing the directory and the ledger.
+- [ ] `Sources/FoundationModelsMultitool/Capabilities/Shell/ShellState.swift:410` `duplication/duplication` — `recordForCrash` repeats the identify-then-record logic of `StdioServerProcess.writeRecord`: look up the live `ProcessIdentity` of a pid, return if it is gone, then write it to the `ProcessLedger` under a key. Add one method on `ProcessLedger`, for example `func recordProcess(key: String, pid: pid_t)`, that performs the `ProcessIdentity.of(pid:)` lookup, the early return, and the best-effort `try?` write. Both `recordForCrash` and `writeRecord` then call it with their own key, and each keeps only its key choice.
